question.text: Saksham Skills Pvt Ltd reports its SIA using the 'Theory of Change' method. Which chain of elements does a Theory of Change map correctly depict?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 7.3.1 states: 'An organisation using the Theory of Change method can express impact in terms of a map showing input, output, outcome and impact.' This is the standard log-frame chain. **The Trap:** A is a P&L chain, C is an investment-analytics chain, D is an accounting identity. Each is tempting for a candidate from a finance background but none is a ToC chain. **Cross-Exam Context:** ToC is used by J-PAL (cited in Ch 7.2.2) and by DIME at the World Bank. Same logic underpins programme-evaluation work in V-B MF Foundation investor-education frameworks. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Pin the Input-Output-Outcome-Impact chain at the top of every ToC workpaper. Challenge any SE indicator that cannot be placed on exactly one rung of this ladder — unplaceable indicators are usually the ones that get trimmed during final-signoff review.
